# Section 1: The Principle of Integrity

Section 1 contains a single standard that is foundational to the entire accreditation process.

## Standard 1.1 — Integrity [CR] {.core-requirement}

::: {.callout-important}
## Core Requirement
This is a Core Requirement — one of the most fundamental aspects of institutional quality.
:::

### What SACSCOC is Trying to Ensure

The institution operates with integrity in all matters. This principle underlies all other standards and expectations.

### Special Note

::: {.callout-note}
## Not Addressed in Compliance Certification
Standard 1.1 is NOT addressed through a narrative in the Compliance Certification. Instead, institutional integrity is evaluated through:

- Conduct throughout the accreditation process
- Accuracy of information provided
- Ethical behavior in all institutional operations
- Proper handling of substantive changes
- Accurate representation of accreditation status
:::

### How Integrity is Demonstrated

- **Honest reporting** in all submissions
- **Ethical behavior** in institutional operations
- **Timely disclosure** of substantive changes
- **Good faith engagement** with the accreditation process
- **Accurate representation** of accreditation status to the public

### Common Concerns

| Issue | Impact |
|-------|--------|
| Submitting inaccurate or misleading information | Integrity finding |
| Failing to report substantive changes | Policy violation |
| Misrepresenting accreditation status | Public trust violation |
| Withholding information from evaluators | Process violation |

### Reflective Prompts

- How do we ensure accuracy in all our SACSCOC submissions?
- Do we have a process for identifying and reporting substantive changes?
- Is our accreditation status accurately stated on our website and publications?
- How do we demonstrate good faith throughout the accreditation process?
